Net profit sits after interest, depreciation and amortization, and taxes. If Brew & Bean funded an aggressive store build-out with debt, you'd see interest expense climb and D&A step up as new stores capitalize leasehold improvements and equipment, and that alone can eat several points of net margin without a single operating cost moving. So the cleaner tree is: net profit equals revenue, minus COGS, minus store operating costs, minus corporate SG&A, minus D&A, minus interest, minus tax.
